reviews.title: Don’t do it.
reviews.text:
I bought these security cameras a few years ago, and the app that came with them had no subscription fee. Then came the push to pay—and ads so intrusive that simply viewing my own cameras has become an absolutely infuriating ordeal.

Many times, I have to completely close and reopen the app several times before an ad finally gives me an X that lets me dismiss it. I should not have to fight through advertisements to access security cameras I already paid for.

Even when I finally get in, pop-ups appear so quickly that I repeatedly click on ads by accident. Those accidental clicks are not interest in the advertised products. They’re the result of an obnoxious interface that makes it difficult to avoid them. It certainly makes me question how meaningful their advertising click numbers are.

This is an incredibly disrespectful way to treat customers. If the free experience is this aggravating, it gives me absolutely no confidence that paying will deliver a better one. I will not reward this behavior with a subscription.

I’ve already begun getting rid of these cameras and switching to another system. You took a customer who had already bought your products and drove him away by making them miserable to use.

My advice: steer clear of this app and the cameras that depend on it.

reviews.title: 1 STAR — SECURITY CAMERAS SHOULD NOT MAKE YOU WATCH ADS
reviews.text:
This is honestly one of the worst purchases I’ve made.

I bought security cameras so I could immediately see what is happening inside or around my home. Instead, when I get an alert and open the YI app, I’m forced to sit through advertisements before I can even access my own camera.

That is absolutely ridiculous.

If someone is entering my home, there is suspicious activity, or something is happening that requires immediate attention, I shouldn’t have to watch multiple ads before I can see what’s going on. By the time the advertisements are finished, the situation could already be over.

I paid for the cameras. I should not have to deal with an advertising obstacle course just to access the product I already purchased.

I understand companies need to make money, but putting ads between a security alert and the camera footage is completely unacceptable. Security cameras are supposed to provide immediate access and peace of mind—not make you wait around while the company tries to sell you something.

The fact that there are multiple ads and subscription prompts makes the experience even worse.

YI needs to understand the difference between monetizing an app and interfering with the fundamental purpose of a security product. If I receive a security alert, let me see my damn camera.

I would not recommend these cameras to anyone looking for a reliable home security system. The advertising alone has made me regret buying them.

reviews.title: A SEVERE SAFETY HAZARD! Do not buy! Held hostage by unskippable ads.
reviews.text:
I originally bought this camera for home security, expecting it to do its basic job: letting me see my home in real-time. However, after recent software updates, this company has turned a critical safety device into a literal ad-player.
Every single time I open the app to check a security alert, I am forced to sit through 5 to 10 seconds of aggressive, unskippable full-screen popup advertisements. Think about it: if there is an intruder, a fire, or a medical emergency at my house, I have to watch a mobile game commercial before I can see the live feed! This is absolutely insane and incredibly dangerous.
The company is deliberately ruining the hardware I already paid for, just to blackmail me into buying their subscription cloud service to remove the ads. This is a classic bait-and-switch.
DO NOT BUY ANY PRODUCTS FROM THIS COMPANY. They care more about squeezing ad revenue out of you than your actual home safety. Look elsewhere for a reliable security brand.

reviews.title: If you’re considering buying a YI Home Camera, don’t. Just don’t.
reviews.text:
I genuinely don’t understand how a security camera system—something meant to protect your home, your family, your safety—can be so aggressively sabotaged by its own app. The number of ads shoved into the experience is beyond ridiculous. It’s not just annoying, it’s negligent.

Every time you open the app, you’re forced to sit through ads like you’re watching a low-budget mobile game, not trying to check on your home. Want to view a live feed? Ad. Want to review footage? Ad. Missed a notification? Good luck—another ad is waiting before you can even see what happened.

Now imagine this: you get an alert in the middle of the night. Something’s wrong. You open the app—heart racing—trying to see what’s going on in your living room. But before anything loads, you’re hit with a full-screen ad. You can’t skip it. Seconds feel like minutes. By the time it finally disappears and the footage loads, it’s too late. You see chaos, you see movement—but the one thing you needed most, the intruder’s face, is gone. Lost in the time you were forced to watch an ad about some random product you didn’t ask for.

That’s not just bad design—that’s a complete failure of the product’s purpose.

Security systems are supposed to prioritize speed, clarity, and reliability. The YI app prioritizes ad revenue. And that trade-off could cost people real peace of mind—or worse.

When I originally bought the camera, there was no mention or need to pay a subscription to an app and the app was useable. They have purposefully made it an awful unusable experience to extract more money from customers. AVOID THIS BRAND AT ALL COSTS.

reviews.title: Camera is great, company is awful.
reviews.text: I want to start with saying I have never written a review on an app, but I have to warn people. The cameras work great. This app and the actually company is awful. The app consistently has adds, even just to open the app. I figure buying the cameras would be enough but it’s not. Unless you buy a premium subscription, not even a regular one, there will be adds on adds. Secondly, if you do purchase a subscription to their service, beware; you have to go out of your way to cancel. You can’t just cancel like you could every other subscription I have had in my life, you have to make a “Cancellation Inquiry”. They take a few days to get back to you about your “Inquiry” just to tell you they can extend your subscription for a lower price or free, but they don’t cancel it. I went back and forth multiple times and they still have not cancelled. Please be wary of this company and their awful customer service. It’s is truly money hungry and shady. I do not recommend.

reviews.title: Horrible - Security with Ads
reviews.text: I’ve had Yi for years. Intentionally to monitor my son when he was younger, then kept them indoors for security purposes. I paid for the MicroSD cards since I didn’t want to pay the monthly/yearly fees. I never had an issue. I could login through the app, watch live. Or review alerts from my memory cards. A few months ago, I noticed Yi started implementing ads. I didn’t mind them because they were just small banners to sign up for their cloud services, but I have the memory cards. Now, the reason for this 1-star is because they’ve put the ads into EVERYTHING. You have an alert, and want to ensure no one’s broken into your home? Or make sure your child isn’t choking on food? No worries, just watch the ads that Yi has forced upon their customers before seeing live footage. Oh you bypassed their ads? Well no worries, Yi now forces you to wait 160 seconds before watching live or pay for their services to avoid it. Same with recorded videos. Once my home is sold, I’m throwing away their cams. Never again will I purchase Yi products. Horrible idea when their products are for security, yet, they want you to pay for their service by forcing ads into your security system.

reviews.title: Disappointing, Greedy

It started with the ads…ok while completely annoying I kinda dealt with it…everyone needs to make a buck right?? But imagine my surprise when after all these years I go to view my feed and learn that unless I subscribe to your services I may only view 9 sec?? I have an adult daughter who is epileptic and medicine resistant and I have always relied on the ability to keep an eye on her if I ever had to leave her alone. Disappointed doesn’t even come close to describing how I feel when after 7 years this is what I’m met with. Factor your costs into the purchase price, don’t slam people with the ultimatum to subscribe to your services or lose your camera feed. Not a real good way to do business especially when there are people out there who rely on the same services they’ve had for nearly a decade. I will make sure everyone who asks for my recommendation knows exactly how I feel. Sad
